properties.name: Oracle of Mount Olympus
properties.summary: Seat of the twelve gods; pilgrims climb here to receive prophecy from the priestesses of Zeus.
properties.summaryRuined: The ancient sanctuary stands silent. Its oracle fires are extinguished, the priestesses gone. Crumbling columns mark where the gods once spoke, and only the wind answers those who call.

properties.name: Sunken Halls of Atlantis
properties.summary: A kingdom swallowed by the sea in a single night. Its towers still stand beneath the waves, and on still days sailors claim to hear bells from below.

properties.name: Parthenon of Athena
properties.summary: The great temple atop the Acropolis, dedicated to Athena the goddess of wisdom, standing in gleaming marble above the city of Athens.
properties.summaryRuined: The marble columns still stand but the roof is long gone, open to the sky Athena once claimed. Pilgrims still leave offerings among the broken stones, though no goddess answers.

properties.name: Palace of Knossos
properties.summary: The legendary labyrinthine palace of King Minos, where the Minotaur waits in the dark for its next tribute of Athenian youth. A thousand rooms and no map.
properties.summaryRuined: The great labyrinth has crumbled. Its passages lie open to the sky, the Minotaur's maze collapsed into rubble. Only faint traces of painted walls survive to suggest what once lived here.

properties.name: Ruins of Troy
properties.summary: The scorched walls of Ilion, sacked after ten years of siege. Only ash and legend remain where Helen once walked.

properties.name: Temple of Karnak
properties.summary: The vast complex of Amun-Ra, where the Nile priests maintain the balance of Ma'at and pharaohs bargain with the gods for eternal life.
properties.summaryRuined: Sand has swallowed the outer courts. The great hypostyle hall still stands but its colors have faded, and the priests of Ra walk these corridors no more. The gods have moved on.

properties.name: Great Pyramid of Osiris
properties.summary: Built as a gateway between the living and the dead, aligned to the stars of Orion so the pharaoh's soul might ascend to Osiris.
properties.summaryRuined: The pyramid still stands — it always will — but its gleaming white limestone casing has been stripped away and the golden capstone is gone. The gateway to Osiris is sealed for good.

properties.name: Underworld Gate of Anubis
properties.summary: A living desert shrine where Anubis holds court over the newly dead, weighing hearts against a feather. Those found heavy vanish into darkness.
properties.summaryRuined: The desert has reclaimed the shrine. Only a scatter of blackened stones marks where Anubis once held court. The scales of judgment have not been seen in an age, but the darkness below remains.

properties.name: Valhalla — Hall of the Slain
properties.summary: Odin's great mead-hall where the bravest warriors feast until Ragnarok. The Valkyries ride at dusk to collect the worthy dead from every battlefield.
properties.summaryRuined: Ragnarok has come and gone. The great hall is ash and collapsed timber. The warriors who feasted here fought their last battle and passed beyond. Even the gods did not survive.

properties.name: Yggdrasil — The World Tree
properties.summary: The immense ash tree whose roots reach into all nine worlds. Odin hung himself from its branches for nine days to discover the runes. It endures all eras.

properties.name: Ruins of Utgard
properties.summary: The fortress of the frost giants at the edge of the world, where Thor was humbled by illusions. The cat he could not lift was the Midgard Serpent itself.

properties.name: Temple of Brahma, Pushkar
properties.summary: One of the few temples dedicated to Brahma the Creator, built beside the sacred lake where a lotus fell from his hand and the world bloomed.

properties.name: Sunken City of Dwarka
properties.summary: The golden city of Krishna, swallowed by the sea the moment he departed the world. Divers still find its towers beneath the waves.

properties.name: Lanka — Ravana's Fortress
properties.summary: The island stronghold of the demon king Ravana, built of gold and guarded by demons. No army has breached its walls — until now.
properties.summaryRuined: Rama's armies burned Lanka to its foundations. The golden towers are charred stumps and the demon king's throne is a pile of rubble. Monkeys have made their home in what remains.

properties.name: Mount Meru — Cosmic Axis
properties.summary: The sacred mountain at the center of the universe, home to the gods. Its peak pierces the heavens and its roots anchor the earth. It has existed since before time.

properties.name: Village of the Pandavas
properties.summary: The humble settlement where the five Pandava princes live in exile, their fate tied to the great war that will decide the age.
properties.summaryRuined: The great war of the Mahabharata left nothing standing here. The village is empty, its paths overgrown, its hearths cold. The age of heroes consumed everything it touched.

properties.name: Ruins of Persepolis
properties.summary: The ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid empire, built to honor Ahura Mazda. Burned by Alexander, its ghosts still walk the Hall of a Hundred Columns.

properties.name: Tower of Silence
properties.summary: A Zoroastrian dakhma where the dead are offered to the sun and the vultures, so the soul may ascend to Ahura Mazda's light unburdened by flesh.
properties.summaryRuined: The dakhma stands abandoned, its sacred fires cold. The vultures have gone elsewhere, and the bones of the dead lie where they fell with no priests to receive them.

properties.name: Palace of Zahhak the Serpent King
properties.summary: The terrifying palace of the tyrant Zahhak, from whose shoulders living serpents grow and demand a daily meal of human brains. The screams are heard for miles.
properties.summaryRuined: Torn down stone by stone when the hero Fereydun freed the world. Nothing remains but a blackened foundation and the smell of old serpent blood that no rain has washed away.

properties.name: Jade Emperor's Temple, Chengdu
properties.summary: A celestial temple where the Jade Emperor receives tribute from all the gods of heaven. His court decides the fate of every living soul.

properties.name: Dragon Gate — Yellow River
properties.summary: The sacred waterfall where carp leap against the current. Any fish that survives the climb transforms into a dragon. Pilgrims come to witness the miracle.
properties.summaryRuined: The sacred waterfall has silenced. No more carp make the leap, no more transformations occur. The bones of failed aspirants have turned to stone in the dry riverbed.

properties.name: Mount Kunlun — Home of Xi Wangmu
properties.summary: The heavenly mountain home of the Queen Mother of the West, whose peach garden grows the fruit of immortality, ripening only once every three thousand years.

properties.name: Forbidden Celestial Palace, Beijing
properties.summary: The earthly reflection of the Jade Emperor's heavenly court, where the Son of Heaven rules as intermediary between the mortal world and the divine.

properties.name: Village of the Eight Immortals
properties.summary: A misty mountain hamlet where the Eight Immortals gather before crossing the sea, each carrying their magical treasure and arguing about who should go first.

properties.name: Izumo Grand Shrine
properties.summary: The oldest and most sacred shrine in Japan. Every October all eight million kami gather here to decide the fates and marriages of mortals for the coming year.

properties.name: Aokigahara — Gate to Yomi
properties.summary: The dense forest at the foot of Mount Fuji where all sound dies and compasses spin uselessly. A crack in the earth here leads down to Yomi, the underworld.

properties.name: Ryūgū-jō — Dragon Palace
properties.summary: The underwater palace of Ryūjin, the dragon god of the sea. A day spent here is a century above. The tidal jewels in his vault control the rise and fall of every ocean.

properties.name: Mount Fuji Shrine — Gateway to Heaven
properties.summary: The sacred peak of Fujisan, where the goddess Konohanasakuya-hime resides among the clouds. Pilgrims climb through the night to greet the gods at the summit sunrise.

properties.name: Village of the Tengu
properties.summary: A remote mountain settlement where the long-nosed Tengu spirits train wandering warriors in secret arts before vanishing with the morning mist.

properties.name: Chichen Itza — Temple of Kukulcan
properties.summary: The pyramid of the feathered serpent god. At each equinox a shadow snake descends its staircase, marking the moment Kukulcan returns to walk among his people.
properties.summaryRuined: The jungle has returned. Roots crack the pyramid's steps and vines drape the serpent carvings. At each equinox locals say the shadow snake still descends — but there is no one left to watch.

properties.name: Tikal — City of the Jaguar Lords
properties.summary: A once-great Maya city swallowed by jungle. Its pyramids pierce the canopy and jaguar priests still walk its plazas at night, performing rites for an empty city.

properties.name: Palenque — Palace of the Sun Shield
properties.summary: Tomb of Pakal the Great, whose sarcophagus lid shows him descending into Xibalba on a world-tree throne. The king is dead but his journey is not finished.

properties.name: Uxmal — House of the Governor
properties.summary: Built overnight by a dwarf who hatched from an egg, on the orders of the rain god Chaac. The governor's house has no equal in the known world.
properties.summaryRuined: The dwarf's pyramid stands but the city around it is jungle. The House of the Governor has no governor, and Chaac receives no more offerings. The drought that followed has not ended.

properties.name: Xibalba — Entrance to the Underworld
properties.summary: The cave entrance to the Maya underworld. The Hero Twins defeated the lords of death in a ball game here. The cold that rises from below has never stopped.

properties.name: Machu Picchu — City in the Clouds
properties.summary: An Inca citadel so high in the Andes that clouds pass through its streets. Its Intihuatana stone is said to tether the sun, keeping it from wandering off course.
properties.summaryRuined: The citadel stands empty, its stone perfectly fitted but its people gone. Llamas graze among the terraces and clouds still pass through the streets of a city with no citizens.

properties.name: Tiwanaku — Gateway of the Sun
properties.summary: The active ceremonial center of the creator god Viracocha, who fashioned humanity from clay at this spot and wept golden tears as he breathed life into them.
properties.summaryRuined: The Gateway of the Sun still stands but the city around it has dissolved into the earth. Viracocha's carved face gazes over a plain of scattered stones and absolute silence.

properties.name: Cuzco — Navel of the World
properties.summary: The sacred capital of the Inca, laid out in the shape of a puma. The Temple of the Sun is sheathed in gold plates that dazzle the eye of Inti himself.
properties.summaryRuined: The shape of the puma city is lost. The gold was stripped from the Temple of the Sun and its walls built over by those who came after. The navel of the world is buried and forgotten.

properties.name: Island of the Sun, Lake Titicaca
properties.summary: The birthplace of the Inca creation myth, where Inti placed the first Inca, Manco Capac, and commanded him to found a civilization worthy of the light.

properties.name: Village of Viracocha
properties.summary: The last place Viracocha the creator god walked among humans before striding into the Pacific Ocean and disappearing. The villagers still leave offerings at the shore.
properties.summaryRuined: Nothing marks the spot where the creator god last walked. The village is gone, its memory preserved only in songs that fewer people sing each generation.

properties.name: Bear Butte — Sacred Mountain of the Lakota
properties.summary: The mountain where Sweet Medicine received the four sacred arrows from Maheo the All-Father — gifts that gave the Cheyenne their laws and their purpose as a people.

properties.name: Cahokia Mounds — City of the Sun People
properties.summary: The greatest city north of Mexico, now abandoned. Its Woodhenge aligned to the solstice, and its mounds are said to hum at midnight with ancestral voices.

properties.name: Mesa Verde — Cliff Palace
properties.summary: A thriving Ancestral Puebloan city carved into the canyon cliff face, its kivas alive with ceremony and its people dancing for rain in the dry season.
properties.summaryRuined: The cliff dwellings stand perfectly preserved but completely empty, abandoned in a single generation. The kivas hold the last prayers of those who danced for rain. They never came back.

properties.name: Serpent Mound — Ohio
properties.summary: A quarter-mile earthwork in the shape of an uncoiling serpent, aligned to the summer solstice sunset. No one is buried here. It was built only to be seen from the sky.

properties.name: Village of the Thunderbird
properties.summary: A Pacific Northwest settlement where the great Thunderbird nests in the mountains above. Its wingbeats make thunder, its eyes flash lightning, and its shadow darkens whole valleys.
